newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Ssangyong may move some assembly to Chin.
newsitem.headline: Ssangyong may move some assembly to Chin.

text.p: Ssangyong Motor Co Ltd, a unit of South Korea's Ssangyong Group, is negotiating the transfer of some production lines to China, a group executive said on Tuesday.

Chang Ki-taek, vice president of the group, said Ssangyong Motor was now discussing with a Chinese partner the relocation to China of part of Ssangyong's assembly lines for large-sized commercial vehicles.

"We are seeking the venture as part of our self-rescue steps. Details will be finalised by the end of this year," Chang said. Other Ssangyong officials said China would provide the company with a huge market and cheap labour.

Ssangyong Motor, saddled with more than three trillion won in debts, has sold its headquarters building to three Ssangyong affiliates to raise cash, a group spokesman said. It is still trying to sell other assets, he said.
Ssangyong, a specialised maker of four wheel-drive utility vehicles, earlier said it wanted to raise some 400 billion won by selling off various assets.
The company's debts snowballed after Ssangyong poured about two trillion won into developing four new models in a technical tie-up with Mercedes-Benz, a subsidiary of Daimler-Benz.
